chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while she was in a state of purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse, and he witnessed with one man on that day, then waited five days, then witnessed with another man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They were only commanded to have both witnesses present together.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having separate witnesses for divorce at different times in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifying that the two witnesses for a divorce pronounced during purity (*al-talaq fi al-tahur*) must be present simultaneously, invalidating sequential witnessing. This ruling emphasizes the formal integrity of the divorce contract in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the act is witnessed as a single, cohesive legal event rather than a fragmented process.
